missionPremise: pePaywallStripe.ts's doc comment above peBillingIntervalForPriceId (verified in this worktree) states this repo deliberately never reads Stripe's current_period_end/plan.interval because their shape moves with the API version and nothing in this repo pins one -- confirmed by grep: zero pre-existing hits for Stripe-Version/STRIPE_API_VERSION anywhere in artifacts/api-server/src, and no `stripe` npm dependency (hand-rolled fetch client only). This is the exact exclusion named in P-125's CP1 (_inbox/2026-09-08_p125_cp1.json, same day, same repo) as deliberately deferred. P-129 is that deferred design, done live rather than stored, and doubles as the data source for the cancellation flow's 'is a cancellation already scheduled' state.
completionPredicate: A live GET route at /property-explorer/v1/subscription, authenticated (requirePeAuthenticated + inner resolvePeOwnerUserId check), resolving the Stripe customer via the SAME function A-062's billing-portal route already uses (readPeStripeCustomerId -- never re-derived, never creates a customer as a side effect of a read), calling Stripe's Subscriptions API live with an explicitly pinned Stripe-Version header for that one call only (stripeGet widened with an additive optional param; its one other caller unaffected), returning ONLY currentPeriodEnd/cancelAtPeriodEnd/status extracted field-by-field (never the raw Stripe object -- proven by a violation test asserting foreign fields do not leak), with every failure mode producing a declared non-2xx or an explicit hasSubscription:false rather than a fabricated date or a silent null-looking 200 (no customer -> 200 false; no LIVE-status subscription -> 200 false; more than one live subscription -> 502, refused not guessed; malformed Stripe response -> 502, refused not coerced; Stripe not configured -> 503, distinct from the 200 absence; Stripe error -> 502 carrying Stripe's own message). MET -- verification below. Client wiring and the portal-replacement decision were explicitly out of this lane's completion bar per the dispatch and are reported, not built.
scopeBasis: Dispatch scoped this lane to ONE route serving both the renewal-date read and the cancellation-flow's status read, built on the existing customer-resolution (readPeStripeCustomerId) and HTTP-client (stripeGet) seams rather than inventing new ones. Explicitly out of scope and NOT touched: the existing hosted Customer Portal redirect (A-062, PE_BILLING_PORTAL_ROUTE) -- investigated and NOT replaced (see stoppedOrFlagged below, this is a recommendation, not a decision made unilaterally); any hauska-map client-side wiring (repo not cloned in this worktree); any Stripe secret or price-id configuration.

routeContract.auth: Session cookie / Bearer token resolving to an authenticated PE user via requirePeAuthenticated (same middleware/session mechanism as every other /property-explorer/v1/* route, e.g. PE_BILLING_PORTAL_ROUTE). No request body, no query params read.

responses.200_no_subscription: { ok: true, hasSubscription: false, stripeConfigured: boolean } -- signed in, no live Stripe subscription (never had one, or the only one on file is not in an active/trialing/past_due/unpaid status)
responses.200_active: { ok: true, hasSubscription: true, status: string, currentPeriodEnd: string (ISO 8601), cancelAtPeriodEnd: boolean, stripeConfigured: true }
responses.503: { error: "subscription_unavailable", message: string, stripeConfigured: false } -- Stripe not configured on this deployment; distinct from the 200 absence -- means "could not check", never rendered as "no renewal"
responses.502: { error: "subscription_check_failed", message: string, stripeConfigured: boolean } -- Stripe answered with an error, returned a subscription missing/mistyping status|current_period_end|cancel_at_period_end (extraction fails closed), or the customer carries more than one concurrently-live subscription (ambiguity refused rather than guessed at)

routeContract.note: hasSubscription is the discriminant a client should branch on FIRST; status/currentPeriodEnd/cancelAtPeriodEnd are only present when hasSubscription is true. stripeConfigured is informational on every 200/503 response. No field carries a raw Stripe object -- every field is individually extracted and type-checked server-side.

stoppedOrFlagged: Client wiring (hauska-map): NOT attempted. hauska-map is not cloned in this worktree and this lane's dispatch explicitly said to stop and report the contract rather than guess at client code that could not be verified. The route contract above (path, method, auth, exact response shapes for all five states) is the handoff for that wiring to be scoped precisely.

Portal-replacement question: NOT decided unilaterally, per the dispatch's explicit instruction that this is a bigger call than the mission should make on its own. Investigation finding, reported as a recommendation: the existing hosted-portal redirect (A-062, PE_BILLING_PORTAL_ROUTE, POST /property-explorer/v1/billing/portal) and this new route serve DIFFERENT purposes -- the portal is where a customer actually manages or cancels a subscription (Stripe's own UI, handles payment-method changes, proration, etc.), while this route is a read used to DISPLAY renewal/cancellation-scheduled facts inline in the product before a customer is sent anywhere. Recommendation: do not replace the portal redirect; wire the cancellation flow to CALL this route first (to show what would be cancelled) and continue to hand off to the portal for the actual cancel action, unless a future card scopes building a fully custom cancel UI against Stripe's Subscriptions API directly (a materially larger change Stripe itself discourages moving off the portal for, given proration/dunning/payment-method edge cases the portal already handles). This is a recommendation for the operator to rule on, not a decision made here.
